description: Team Fable 7.0 (Dhaka) presents BD-FireOps for NASA Space Apps 2026. We harmonize 20 years of MODIS (1km) and VIIRS (375m) fire records over Bangladesh CHT. Skills: Earth Observation, Machine Learning, Remote Sensing, and Web GIS to build open-source tools for climate science and the Bangladesh Forest Department.
summary: NASA projects the retirement of Terra and Aqua MODIS in 2027, while Suomi-NPP VIIRS data delivery ceased on 1 November 2026. Merging 1 km MODIS and 375 m VIIRS active-fire records creates an artificial +185% jump over Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT). BD-FireOps bridges this sensor gap. Using an Aqua MODIS reference baseline, time-split empirical modeling (2012–2018 train, 2019–2021 held-out test), and a 500-sample moving-block bootstrap interval, BD-FireOps cuts held-out prediction error (RMSE) by 95.1% and reduces mean sensor bias by 99.1%. An unchanged Aqua MODIS control test confirms actual burning fell 23.1% across the boundary, proving the historical surge was an artifact of camera resolution. Deployed as an open-access Web GIS dashboard, BD-FireOps provides forest rangers, hill communities, and researchers with an uncertainty-quantified 20-year monthly fire baseline and live 6-hourly NOAA-20/21 satellite monitoring.
details:
### 1. How It Works

BD-FireOps is an open-source, uncertainty-aware Earth observation engine that bridges the historical discontinuity between NASA EOS MODIS and SNPP VIIRS active-fire sensors across Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT).

- **Quality-Assurance Pipeline:** Filters raw NASA FIRMS detections to the CHT bounding box (91.9°–92.9°E, 21.4°–23.8°N), clips strictly within Bandarban, Rangamati, and Khagrachhari district polygons via geoBoundaries BGD-ADM2, deduplicates observations, and filters confidence (MODIS ≥ 30, dropping VIIRS low-confidence 'l' flags).

- **Aqua MODIS Reference Gating:** Restricts the reference series to Aqua afternoon overpasses (~13:30 local) to align with Suomi-NPP equator crossings, avoiding diurnal cycle bias.

- **Empirical Harmonization:** Fits an ordinary least squares model on the 2012–2018 overlap (84 months) and evaluates on an untouched 36-month held-out test set (2019–2021).

- **Uncertainty Quantification:** Generates 95% coefficient intervals via a 500-sample moving-block bootstrap (12-month contiguous blocks to respect fire seasonality).

### 2. Validation & Scientific Proof

- **Error & Bias Reduction:** Held-out RMSE drops by 95.1% (from 1,130.64 to 55.67 hotspots/month) and mean sensor bias drops by 99.1% (from +468.92 to -4.09), achieving test R² = 0.9811 and Spearman rank correlation ρ = 0.9488.

- **The Control Test:** Aqua MODIS, an instrument with unchanged optics throughout 2002–2021, recorded a -23.1% decline across the 2012 boundary, mathematically proving that the raw +185% surge was a sensor artifact rather than a physical fire surge.

### 3. Benefits & Impact

- **Forest Department & Rangers:** Rapid district triage (*Where to look first*) ranks fire activity against historical baselines, allowing targeted ranger deployment.

- **Hill Farming Communities:** Plain-language seasonal guidance and jhum burning safety tips without inflating indigenous farming activity.

- **Climate Scientists:** A unified, uncertainty-bounded 20-year monthly record with one-click CSV export.

### 4. Tools & Technologies

- **Data & Modeling:** Python 3.10+, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy, matplotlib.

- **Web GIS & Dashboard:** HTML5, CSS3 (zero-repaint GPU composited layers), Vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet 1.9.4, Chart.js 4.4.1.

- **CI/CD & Deployment:** GitHub Actions (automated 6-hourly live FIRMS ingest and 104-check audit test suite), hosted on Vercel.
